title: Thailand's Aging Society
topic: ข่าว/สังคม (ข้อมูล)
lines: Thailand is aging faster than almost any other country in Asia. In 2000,
about one in ten Thais was over sixty. Today **that** number is one in five,
and by 2040 experts expect it to be one in three. The main reasons are
longer lives and falling birth rates: Thai women now have, on average,
just one child each, compared with six in the 1960s.
This change brings serious challenges. Fewer young workers will have to
support more retired people, and hospitals will need more staff trained
to care for **them**. In rural areas, **many** elderly people already live
alone because their children have moved to cities for work.
Some communities are finding creative solutions. In one village in
Chiang Rai, retired teachers run a "school for the elderly," where older
people learn to use smartphones, exercise together and share skills.
**Its** organizers say loneliness has dropped sharply. Experts believe
projects like **this** will become more important in the coming years.
